claims.title: The Sacred City of Caral-Supe
claims.summary: On the central coast the monumental city of Caral rises, with pyramids and sunken plazas, among the oldest urban centres of the Americas and the heart of the Norte Chico tradition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-3000bce-the-sacred-city-of-caral-supe, claim TL:PER:event:3000bce:the-sacred-city-of-caral-supe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of Chavin de Huantar
claims.summary: The highland temple of Chavin de Huantar becomes a centre of pilgrimage and oracle, spreading a powerful religious art and ideology across the central Andes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-900bce-rise-of-chavin-de-huantar, claim TL:PER:event:900bce:rise-of-chavin-de-huantar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moche and Nazca cultures
claims.summary: The Moche of the north coast create realistic pottery and adobe pyramids, while the Nazca of the southern deserts inscribe their giant lines and geoglyphs.

sources.label: Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Pampas de Jumana

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-100-moche-and-nazca-cultures, claim TL:PER:event:100:moche-and-nazca-cultures, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Wari state
claims.summary: From the Ayacucho region the Wari build an expansive state with roads and planned centres, prefiguring the imperial methods later used by the Inca.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-600-the-wari-state, claim TL:PER:event:600:the-wari-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pachacuti transforms the Inca state
claims.summary: After defending Cusco against the Chanca, Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui takes power and begins the swift expansion that turns the kingdom of Cusco into the empire of Tawantinsuyu.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1438-pachacuti-transforms-the-inca-state, claim TL:PER:event:1438:pachacuti-transforms-the-inca-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Building of Machu Picchu
claims.summary: The Inca raise the mountain sanctuary of Machu Picchu above the Urubamba, a masterpiece of stonework later recognised as a World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1450-building-of-machu-picchu, claim TL:PER:event:1450:building-of-machu-picchu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Empire at its height
claims.summary: Under Pachacuti's successors the Inca extend Tawantinsuyu from present-day Colombia to Chile and Argentina, bound by roads, storehouses and the mita labour system.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1471-empire-at-its-height, claim TL:PER:event:1471:empire-at-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Inca civil war
claims.summary: A ruinous war of succession between the half-brothers Atahualpa and Huascar divides the empire just as the Spanish appear on its coasts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1529-inca-civil-war, claim TL:PER:event:1529:inca-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Atahualpa at Cajamarca
claims.summary: Francisco Pizarro's small force seizes the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca after massacring his escort, a decisive stroke in the conquest of Peru.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1532-capture-of-atahualpa-at-cajamarca, claim TL:PER:event:1532:capture-of-atahualpa-at-cajamarca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Atahualpa
claims.summary: After paying a vast ransom in gold and silver, Atahualpa is executed by the Spanish; with the emperor dead, Pizarro advances on Cusco, taken later that year.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1533-execution-of-atahualpa, claim TL:PER:event:1533:execution-of-atahualpa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Lima
claims.summary: Pizarro founds Lima, the City of Kings, on the coast; it becomes the capital of the future Viceroyalty of Peru, chosen over Cusco for its links to Spain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1535-founding-of-lima, claim TL:PER:event:1535:founding-of-lima, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Viceroyalty of Peru established
claims.summary: Spain creates the Viceroyalty of Peru, second of its American viceroyalties, governing most of Spanish South America from Lima for nearly three centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1542-viceroyalty-of-peru-established, claim TL:PER:event:1542:viceroyalty-of-peru-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The silver of Potosi
claims.summary: The opening of the great silver mountain of Potosi makes Peru the crown's richest American realm, worked through the forced-labour mita that consumes Indigenous lives.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1545-the-silver-of-potosi, claim TL:PER:event:1545:the-silver-of-potosi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolt of Tupac Amaru II
claims.summary: Jose Gabriel Condorcanqui, taking the name Tupac Amaru II, leads a vast Indigenous uprising against Spanish rule across the southern Andes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1780-revolt-of-tupac-amaru-ii, claim TL:PER:event:1780:revolt-of-tupac-amaru-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Tupac Amaru II
claims.summary: Captured by the Spanish, Tupac Amaru II is forced to witness the deaths of his family and is then executed at Cusco; the rebellion is suppressed but remembered.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1781-execution-of-tupac-amaru-ii, claim TL:PER:event:1781:execution-of-tupac-amaru-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence proclaimed by San Martin
claims.summary: Having entered Lima, Jose de San Martin proclaims the independence of Peru and becomes its Protector, though Spanish armies still hold the highlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-proclaimed-by-san-martin, claim TL:PER:event:1821:independence-proclaimed-by-san-martin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Junin
claims.summary: Bolivar's forces win a cavalry battle at Junin, opening the way to the final campaign against the royalists in the Peruvian sierra.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1824-battle-of-junin, claim TL:PER:event:1824:battle-of-junin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Ayacucho
claims.summary: Antonio Jose de Sucre defeats the main royalist army and captures the viceroy at Ayacucho, sealing the independence of Peru and the new South American republics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1824-battle-of-ayacucho, claim TL:PER:event:1824:battle-of-ayacucho, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The guano boom
claims.summary: Exports of coastal guano as fertiliser bring the Peruvian state a vast but poorly managed windfall, funding reforms including the abolition of slavery in 1854.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1840-the-guano-boom, claim TL:PER:event:1840:the-guano-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War of the Pacific
claims.summary: Allied with Bolivia, Peru fights Chile over the nitrate-rich Atacama; Chilean forces occupy Lima in 1881 and Peru is defeated.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1879-war-of-the-pacific, claim TL:PER:event:1879:war-of-the-pacific, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Ancon
claims.summary: Peru cedes Tarapaca to Chile and loses control of Tacna and Arica, a humiliating settlement whose final terms were not fixed until 1929.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1883-treaty-of-ancon, claim TL:PER:event:1883:treaty-of-ancon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Leguia era
claims.summary: Augusto Leguia governs Peru for eleven increasingly authoritarian years, promoting public works and a new constitution before falling in the Depression.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1919-the-leguia-era, claim TL:PER:event:1919:the-leguia-era, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Aprista movement
claims.summary: Victor Raul Haya de la Torre founds the American Popular Revolutionary Alliance (APRA), a mass movement for social reform that shapes Peruvian politics for decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1924-founding-of-the-aprista-movement, claim TL:PER:event:1924:founding-of-the-aprista-movement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Velasco and the military reforms
claims.summary: General Juan Velasco Alvarado leads a leftist military government that enacts sweeping agrarian reform and nationalisations before being eased from power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1968-velasco-and-the-military-reforms, claim TL:PER:event:1968:velasco-and-the-military-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Shining Path launches its insurgency
claims.summary: As civilian democracy is restored, the Maoist Shining Path under Abimael Guzman begins an armed insurrection in the Ayacucho highlands, opening two decades of internal conflict.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1980-shining-path-launches-its-insurgency, claim TL:PER:event:1980:shining-path-launches-its-insurgency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Abimael Guzman
claims.summary: Police capture the Shining Path leader Abimael Guzman in Lima; he is sentenced to life imprisonment and the insurgency is broken.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-1992-capture-of-abimael-guzman, claim TL:PER:event:1992:capture-of-abimael-guzman, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission report
claims.summary: The Commission estimates that some 69,000 people died or disappeared in the 1980-2000 conflict, attributing most deaths to the Shining Path while also documenting state abuses.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-2003-truth-and-reconciliation-commission-report, claim TL:PER:event:2003:truth-and-reconciliation-commission-report, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Impeachment of Pedro Castillo
claims.summary: President Pedro Castillo is impeached and detained after attempting to dissolve Congress; Vice President Dina Boluarte succeeds him amid deadly protests.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Peru: From Caral and the great Andean civilisations to the Inca empire of Tawantinsuyu, the Spanish conquest and the silver of the Viceroyalty, independence secured at Ayacucho in 1824, the War of the Pacific, the internal armed conflict with the Shining Path, and a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/PER/chronicle#ev-2022-impeachment-of-pedro-castillo, claim TL:PER:event:2022:impeachment-of-pedro-castillo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
